MRK.rationale: MRK's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings deterioration: net income swung to -$4.24B (EPS -$1.72) from +$5.08B (EPS +$2.01) YoY, driven by a ~$5.8B one-time charge related to the Terns Pharmaceuticals acquisition. While revenue grew 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, operating income collapsed to -$3.53B. The stock has rallied ~43% over the past year (from ~$84 to ~$120), pushing the P/E to 33.3x—near the top of its 365-day range (11.1–33.9x) and a massive premium to its historical average of ~12–15x. This valuation expansion has occurred despite: (1) the looming Keytruda patent cliff in 2028–2029, which accounts for ~49% of revenue; (2) Gardasil sales declining 22% YoY in Q1; (3) generic headwinds from Januvia/Janumet expected mid-2026; and (4) a $2.5B headwind from generic competition and Medicare pricing pressures in 2026. The balance sheet shows rising liabilities ($82.75B vs $77.64B in equity) declining equity declining declining topably to $. While the pipeline (Winrevair, Capvaxive) and new product launches provide long-term optionality, the market near-term catalyst is limited. The stock is now trading at a3x its historical P/E, with no clear fundamental fundamental catalyst to re-rate it higher. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.603) but the quantitative elevated valuation makes the risk/reward skewed unfavorable.
